slides.title: Where we are
items: On Tuesday we got the motor turning. You wired the TB6612, set its direction by hand, and then ran a program that ramped the speed up and down while you watched the duty cycle change on the oscilloscope.
You also found the timer settings: PA7 is TIM14_CH1 on alternate function 4, and to get 1.6 kHz in 1250 steps from a 12 MHz clock we divide by 6 and count to 1250.
Today we look at all register settings in more detail.
We'll use the reference manual, the figures, and the code.
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 3 min with announcements. 50 minutes today, which is short: the Parts are budgeted to 46 and the rest is settling and transitions. Ask everyone to open RM0490 now, before Part 2 needs it.
